requirements.statement: `/create-trd <prd> --design docs/ui/<slug> --boards <ids>` builds and approves exactly the named boards, using the `/plan --design --boards` rules: a named board that is not buildable is STUCK naming it and its status; a board held by a draft part is STUCK naming the part. Without `--boards`, behaviour is unchanged. MUST-PASS.
requirements.source: TRD §Objectives, O1 (from investigation O1, issue #68 change 1)

requirements.statement: `/create-design` keeps item ids that arrive in its source (a brief listing `S1: Cart`, `S2: Address` keeps `S1`, `S2`); it assigns `BI-n` only when the source has none.

Each board in `design-map.json` records the brief items it serves as `brief_items` (array of item ids), written by `/create-design` and kept current by `/refine-design`; `design-map.js validate` accepts the field and rejects a non-array. MUST-PASS (marked by investigation, unconfirmed by owner).

`design-map.js` lists boards serving given items: `buildable --items S2,S3` returns buildable to-be boards whose `brief_items` include any named item; an item no board serves is reported, not silently dropped. MUST-PASS (marked by investigation, unconfirmed by owner).
`/audit-design`'s traceability verifier reads `brief_items` from the map, so 'a brief item with no board' and 'a board with no brief item' are decided from the recorded field, not a model's reading.

Under `--auto`, `/create-design` and `/refine-design` still produce open decisions and record each in `brief.md` under the fixed heading `## Decisions taken by default`, each with an id (`OD-1`, ...), question, options, option taken, and why; the readout lists them by id in DECISIONS (ISSUES when weak). MUST-PASS (marked by investigation, unconfirmed by owner).
`/refine-design <slug> --auto "OD-2: <option>"` applies an answer to a recorded decision: redraws the boards the decision affects and records the answer against that decision in `brief.md`.
`/refine-design --auto` with no other feedback takes the open findings from the latest `.trd-state/<slug>/audit-design-report.md` as its feedback.

`/audit-build` and `/close-feature` word the `/sync-design` NEXT step so running it now, on the feature branch before merge, is allowed ('now, or once the PR has merged'), and `/sync-design` states it may run on a feature branch.
No shipped text added by this change names a particular product or orchestrator; every change is worded for any unattended caller.
requirements.source: TRD §Objectives, O10 (owner statement in investigation Decision section)

open_questions: OQ-1: Should --auto cap open decisions at four like the interactive round? Assumed: no cap under --auto (a cap would drop decisions silently, which O6 forbids). If wrong: change the AUTO ? all : first four branch in DORCH-B002.
OQ-2: Is a bad OD-n reference (unknown id, option not listed) STUCK or an ISSUES line? Assumed: ISSUES line naming the ids or options that exist; run continues. If wrong: switch D9 to STUCK.

OQ-3: When /sync-design runs on a feature branch, should shipped_commit be re-pointed after merge? Assumed: no, out of scope (TR1). If wrong: drift checks on squash-merged designs point at unreachable commits; needs its own change.

OQ-4: Should the board side of traceability (a board with no brief item) cover part, as-is and flow boards? Assumed: to-be boards only, not superseded. If wrong: an as-is board serving nothing goes unreported.
OQ-5: Should concurrent features coordinate writes to one design-map.json? Assumed: not addressed (TR2). If wrong: merge conflicts in the map need a separate change.
OQ-6: What counts as a weak default? Assumed: the brief agent's own weak flag (D7). If wrong: a caller wanting a stricter rule needs a stated threshold, which nobody has given.

OQ-7: Which lines of the audit report are open findings? Assumed: every finding line except REJECTED THESE FINDINGS, the CAVEAT line and ## Could Not Verify (D10). If wrong: a finding under an unexpected heading is missed or wrongly taken.
